chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Willie Smith passing for white and Lunceford's Fisk education
summary: Crawford says nobody in the band cared that Willie Smith looked white, and he went where the others could not.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And he was a very light-skinned guy.
He went to Fiske, too, didn't he?

Fiske, yeah, he finished Fiske. That was a big school down South. Lunceford finished Fiske, Wilcox finished Fiske. I think I told you that Nelson went to Columbia for post-graduate work. I was just reading where he went -- it was City College. At City College, instead of -- that's beside the point, anyway. He was a great athlete, and a great leader of men.
Well, now, but we've got to jump from -- we still got to get Willie Smith straight.
He was -- now, was there -- let me ask you this. During that period, was there much made about him being light?
No. For some reason, not to us.
No, what I mean is, like, in terms of travelling with the band.

No. Nobody said anything to anybody in that band about him. We were just all buddies. Good whisky drinkers. He was, and I was, quite a few of us. Anyone else you'd like to talk about? We still on Willie?
Yeah, what I mean is, like, you never had any problems, like from white people mistaking him for white or anything like that?
No. He'd go around to places that we couldn't go in. Fool around with white girls that we couldn't make. No, we never had any problem.
But, now, when he would be going around to these places, did people know that he wasn't white, or would he be passing?
